newsitem.title: USA: USDA sharply raises 1997 U.S. pork exports.
newsitem.headline: USDA sharply raises 1997 U.S. pork exports.

text.p: The Agriculture Department on Friday sharply increased its 1997 export forecast for U.S. pork to 1.365 billion lbs, up from last month's estimate of 1.110 billion and compared to last year's exports of 951 million lbs.
The USDA said U.S. pork exports will jump due to an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in Taiwan's hog herds.
"The United States is expected to export more pork as a result of disease problems in Taiwan that have crippled their exports," USDA said in its April supply and demand report.
USDA said the U.S. pork industry is expected to "gain the lion's share" of fresh product that Taiwan would have exported and part of the frozen product market.
The increased exports are expected to tighten domestic supplies and push hog and pork prices higher.
Pork price forecasts for the second half of the year were increased by USDA.
